articleTitle: Characterization and analysis of chain-link fences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A program was initiated to characterize a chain-link fence using a time-dependent three-dimensional vibration analysis in order to provide a better understanding of the effects of the physical characteristics as well as the motion of the fence structure. The primary goals of the analysis were to develop a series of test procedures which would duplicate cutting and climbing attempts, and to develop a clear understanding of the fence construction requirements in order to reduce the nuisance alarm rates due to the varying environmental conditions. The theoretical and experimental analysis took account of wind velocity and other environmental noise, as well as the fence construction. A discussion is presented of the theoretical analysis and the experimental results of the program. Commercial fence sensors were compared to sensitive accelerometers. The results indicate that the commercial sensors are most sensitive at low frequencies. They could not be used to detect some of the high-frequency events which might be useful for distinguishing intrusion attempts from nuisance alarms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer security: a consequence of information technology quality
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A discussion is presented of software security metrics, risk management, qualitative and quantitative methods, and security economics. Particular emphasis is given to software quality as a unifying principle. Several examples of the economic impact of security are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model-based vision for automatic alarm interpretation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: In a previous paper T.J. Ellis et al. (1989) described the development of a knowledge-based vision recognition system for automating the interpretation of alarm events resulting from a perimeter intrusion detection system (PIDS). Measurements extracted over a sequence of digitized images are analyzed to identify the cause of alarm. Models are maintained for both alarm causes and the scene and the measurements are matched with the models to derive an appropriate classification of the event. The authors record progress on the further development of the system and present the results of applying it to a number of real alarms. The system is shown to behave robustly, correctly classifying genuine alarm events (i.e., human intruders) and providing statistics of false alarm events.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image surveillance systems: some novel design features
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: Considerable advances in image storage techniques are now making possible systems for the capture of image sequences showing the scene before, at, and after the time at which a PIDS (perimeter intrusion detection system) is triggered. Novel design features aimed at enhancing the overall performance of the imaging system with cost saving implications are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Observations on the application of error correcting codes to public key encryption
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: With the breaking of the iterated Knapsack algorithm and the realization that the modular arithmetic required by the RSA algorithm causes it to operate slowly, the need for a strong, high speed public key algorithm has increased. The author draws attention to a high speed coding based algorithm. He briefly describes the algorithm in its original form, and then discusses some additional capabilities. These capabilities include the ability to simultaneously correct communication channel errors and to transmit secondary messages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mobile intrusion detection and assessment system (MIDAS)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A description is presented of MIDAS, the Mobile Intrusion Detection and Assessment System. MIDAS is a security system that can be quickly deployed to provide wide area coverage for a mobile asset. MIDAS uses two passive infrared imaging sensors, one for intruder detection and one for assessment. Detected targets are tracked while assessment cameras are directed to view the intruder location for operator observation and assessment. The dual sensor design allows simultaneous detection, assessment, and tracking. Control and status information is provided to an operator using a color graphics terminal, touch panel driven menus, and a joystick for control of the assessment sensor pan and tilt.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A target cueing and tracking system (TCATS) for smart video processing
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: The general-purpose Target Cueing and Tracking System (TCATS) was developed to be independent of the application and the user interface. TCATS has successfully demonstrated a high detection capability and the ability to ignore exterior environmental conditions, such as cloud shadows moving through the scene, snow, blowing dust, rain, and moderate camera motion. TCATS can handle many targets and retain the identity of each object from one frame to the next. Special ruggedized hardware has been developed to reduce the size, cost, and power consumption, and to increase the processing rate, reliability, and environmental operating capability of the TCATS. TCATS is undetectable to an outside intruder. The nature of TCATS would make it difficult for an intruder to defeat, even if the intruder were aware of its existence. Field evaluations are underway for exterior fixed site security applications. A description is given of the TCATS algorithms, custom developed hardware, and preliminary field test results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fiber optic barrier integrity monitor
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A description is presented of two designs for monitoring the integrity of a barrier surrounding a location. The concept was originally developed for verifying compliance to a treaty where the barrier was to surround a site containing treaty-limited items. The application of these designs is not limited to treaty verification and might be used to monitor the integrity of vault walls, building and igloo walls, truck and transport container walls, or net barriers partitioning a harbor. The barrier consists of a row of upright columns supporting three horizontal rails. An optical fiber is threaded through the rails and the continuity of the fiber is monitored via a light signal sent through it. The design is intended to detect any breach immediately so that the violator might be caught in the violation act. The equipment should also detect attempts to tamper with the system by inserting a bypass around a portion of the fiber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A satellite interference location system using differential time and phase measurement techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A description is given of the design and development of a system for inferring the position of terrestrial satellite uplink stations using existing domestic satellites with minimal disruption to normal satellite operation. Two methods are presented by which a quantity measured at a terrestrial receiving site is mapped into a curve of possible uplink locations on the Earth's surface. One method involves measuring differential time delays of a single uplink signal observed through two adjacent spacecraft. Another method uses a short baseline interferometer composed of the two cross-polarized and spatially separated antenna feeds aboard an affected satellite. A unique location is obtained by employing an appropriate combination of the two presented methods. A system for measurement of the required differential delays and phases is described in addition to experimental work performed to demonstrate the feasibility of these location methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction of big seismic waves by optical interferometric antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: This report presents the basic analysis on the prediction of large seismic waves. Seismic waves can be detected by an interferometric gravitational wave antenna before their acoustic arrival, and can therefore be used in prediction. When an earthquake has a magnitude of M/sub S/ approximately 7, the gravitational deviation induces a strain in the antenna arm which is about ten times larger than the noise strain generated by random gravitational forces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Countermeasures selection and integration: a delicate balancing act for the security designer
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: Consideration is given to the structured decision process employed by the design engineer in selecting from a wide range of available physical, electronic, operational, and procedural countermeasures during initial and subsequent system design phases. The countermeasures selection process is examined, along with countermeasures selection and integration. Facility-specific countermeasures are examined. Finally, a discussion is presented of countermeasures cost-effectiveness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Chinese seal identification
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: The identification of Chinese seal imprints is addressed. In seal identification the foundation rests on two points: one is the characteristic features of the seal and the other is the spatial relation of strokes of the seal. A discussion is presented of current identification methods, and computational methods are proposed which could solve large-scale problems involving thresholding, rotation thinning, reexpansion, and matching of seal images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exit-access control in an airport environment
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: It is shown that the first step in defining and developing a successful approach to air travel security and safety is to examine and address the typical airport. Potential areas of vulnerability include baggage and freight cargo as well as preplanted weapons from service or maintenance areas. Exotic weapons, such as chemical or biological weapons, must also be considered as threats. Stand-off weapons from commuter or private aircraft areas, parking lots, or freight delivery areas are also viable threats. The author focuses on an approach and methodology developed for the Baltimore-Washington International Airport threat problem that includes personnel and carry-on luggage in particular. This approach offers increased effectiveness through direct focus on system and facility vulnerabilities and increased efficiency through its adaptability to local needs, operations, and conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Secure data communication in local area networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A secure data exchange (SDE) protocol to provide data confidentiality for secure data communication between two authorized end user systems in an IEEE 802 Local Area Network (LAN) environment is presented. In the development of this protocol, the various primitives used and parameters included in them are given. Also, the secure transmission and reception of these primitives between peer layer entities of source and destination end user systems are presented to achieve data confidentiality security service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Challenges to systems security design caused by a dynamic threat environment
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A discussion of the challenges to system security design caused by the current dynamic threat environment is presented from an experimental standpoint. Particular emphasis is placed on the security design for advanced systems and how the system's own digital features can meet the changing threat. The approach of this work is driven by the threat rather than by government regulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic switching system for high-resolution phototelegraphic equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: In order to effectively utilize fingerprint, facial, and site photographic information, an automatic switching system for high-resolution phototelegraphic equipment was introduced. In this system, phototelegraphs can be sent to many places at one time, and transmission modes such as normal/urgent/special urgent can be set. To transmit data smoothly and efficiently, the system is equipped with functions allowing the most appropriate transmission scheduling, by address, transmission mode, available line and other information. In addition to making it easier to conduct fast searches for runaways and suspects, this system speeds up fingerprint registration and retrieval by making it possible to select a high resolution (20 lines/mm) mode. Quality of this level is necessary for input into the automated Fingerprint Identification System (FIS) developed by National Police Agency. A description is given of the structure, functions, and operation of this Automatic Switching System for High-resolution Phototelegraphic Equipment (ASSP).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of IKBS techniques to perimeter intrusion detection systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: Work concerned with identifying the areas to which application of IKBS (intelligent knowledge-based system) techniques could best benefit the UK's Home Branch and its customers is discussed. Perimeter security was identified as one area in which both the use of rule induction techniques and the incorporation of local rules were likely to be of considerable benefit. An extensive collaborative program with industry was initiated. This work has led to the production of a bespoke hardware system, now the subject of extensive operational trials. The prototype operational study is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evidence gathering and projection devices using new technology for the New Denver International Airport
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A discussion is presented of the evidence gathering and protection devices integrated into the security design standards, the preliminary security design, and the design development phase of the New Denver International Airport. The security analysis and design include evidence gathering and protection devices, analysis security operations, as well as lessons learned from the Stapleton International Airport in Denver, CO. The purpose of the security design standards document is to present an integrated security system design criteria for the Denver International Airport that would result in security design features and operations capable of delivering maximum protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: External intrusion detection systems for critical facilities
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A description is presented of the application of Sparton sensors and systems to perimeter intrusion detection around high-security military and civilian facilities. The system is primarily concerned with protection of approach areas, and assumes that other equipment or systems will be used for detection and identification within the physical boundaries of the secured facility. While Sparton equipment is designed for detection in open areas some sensors are quite suitable for internal detection as well. The system described is based on protection of a hypothetical power plant, and is chosen to illustrate how specific sensors can be used. Other facilities, such as military bases, precious or dangerous material storage areas, or national security buildings could utilize similar sensors. Using radio links, these systems can protect much larger areas such as airfields or national borders.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: White paper on Acme manufacturing plant operations and inventory key assets protection and recovery system
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A solution to dramatically curtail both 'insider' and 'outsider' property theft and diversion problems may be both available and affordable. A Key Assets Protection and Recovery System is proposed. The system integrates advances in microprocessors, machine readers, image processing, fast data finding technology, and computer-based automation to produce a prototype system for use throughout Acme's worldwide operations. It comprises an electronic article surveillance system, communications, a pass and identification system, and an investigations support system. These elements can be designed and built from the outset or added together separately as the local situation demands. Elements of the Key Assets Protection and Recovery System can vary from the simple to the very complex, depending on the specific situation's particular requirements, existing equipment and communication links, current data bases and watchlists, the number of records to be processed, and a variety of other risk/benefits trades.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sensor technology and signal analysis: High security encryption supervision
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: An examination is made of the current approaches to sensor line supervision and their relative effectiveness against the range of easily available circumvention techniques is assessed, compared to encrypted line supervision. Features of high security encrypted line supervision, including encryption techniques, interactive polling, the generation of random data, proprietary algorithms and keys, serial numbers and the processing of such an approach are discussed, including the flexibility offered by miniaturization of the microprocessor controlled circuits and modular system design. How an encryption module can be deployed within an overall high security system is highlighted. Examples of practical applications provide insight into the effective and efficient use of this advanced security technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: When a password is not a password (computer resource security)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: This study focuses on the less obvious vulnerabilities of information systems and the philosophy and technology behind two-factor identification, authentication, and access control systems. How two-factor systems can be technically overlaid for implementation in existing environments is addressed. The theoretical issues associated with using ignition keys stored in tokens versus transmitting them in both clear text and encrypted form are discussed. Guidelines for securing computer resources are presented. Two-factor identification is discussed along with token-based ID authentication. Open networks and secure passwords, are also examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a secure packet voice communication system in wide area networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: The design issues related to the voice packet construction, encryption, transmission, decryption, and reconstruction of original speech signals for secure packet voice communication between source and destination end user systems in a packet switched wide area network are presented. A data encryption standard (DES) algorithm is used for encryption and decryption of voice packets and the public key cryptographic algorithm is used for session key distribution using a key distribution center. These issues may be considered for use in the design of a secure packet voice communication system in wide area networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New technologies in credit card authentication
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: A description is presented of a card for accessing information indirectly using only a bar code. An intelligent card reader is required to retrieve information regarding the cardholder. Magnetic stripe memories are sufficiently large to hold name, number, and about 50 b of reference information for signature verification. Signature verification using dynamic features has been realized with a higher accuracy than that achieved by visual inspection. It appears that a battery-powered single chip microprocessor card reader, and piezoelectric pad for recording the signature dynamics can be combined into a low cost unit. This unit could replace the present roller-printing device. The large number of these units which are required will reduce their cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application and limitations of advanced technologies in explosives detection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: The technological issues involved in advanced explosives, energetic materials, and contraband detection are addressed. To facilitate an appreciation and understanding the problem, a general overview of the chemistry and physics of common and unconventional military and commercial explosive and energetic materials is presented. A discussion is presented of the general approaches, methodologies, and limitations of explosives and energetic materials detection including various forms of radiographic imaging and analytical techniques and future trends in explosives and energetic material detection technology that may be applicable to the international air transportation industry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The computer security framework
publicationTitle: IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology, Crime Countermeasures
abstract: The organization and maintenance of a security framework constitutes a challenge for every company. The author describes the element of such a framework: objectives, conditions, measures and rules which in nature may be organizational, technical, personal, etc. Security guidelines are presented for physical security, security against water damage, lightning and overvoltage protection, protection of the power supply, and disaster recovery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
